core.title: Security tests assert on denial
core.given: A test whose bound URN carries a security kind segment — SEC, RLS or AUTH (the URN binding declared in the file, not the filename, is authoritative).
core.when: Writing, changing or reviewing that security test.
core.then: Prove the refusal named by the security acceptance: for the unauthorized or under-privileged stimulus it describes, assert the denial signal produced by the bound protected operation (e.g. an authentication or authorisation failure status such as 401 or 403, a permission error, a rejection, or a thrown error).
prefer: Construct the missing, invalid or insufficient authorization state the acceptance describes; exercise the real protected boundary.

Required witness when the acceptance protects a mutation or other side effect: also assert that the protected state/action remains unchanged — a denial status returned after performing the mutation is still a security failure.
A happy-path case is optional and welcome, but cannot replace the denial case.
avoid: A happy-path permission case as the only security proof.
An unrelated or generic denial assertion not produced by the bound protected operation, added merely to satisfy the automated check.
Mocking away the authorization decision the acceptance must prove.
For a protected mutation/side effect, asserting only the denial status without checking that the effect did not occur.
core.why: A happy-path-only security test is a silent green gap: it passes CI and counts as covering the security acceptance while proving nothing about the denial path, the only path the acceptance is about.
evidence: The test body contains an expectation tied to a denial signal on the protected operation named by the security acceptance.
The case would turn red if authorization were accidentally removed.
Where the acceptance protects a mutation or side effect (mandatory there), the test shows a denied request cannot still perform the protected effect.
verification: Scope: only tests whose URN carries a security kind segment (SEC, RLS or AUTH) are checked; identification is by the URN bound in the file, not by filename — the URN binding is authoritative (its concrete syntax comes from the profile).
Scope: every such security test, regardless of whether it was changed in the current diff or of lifecycle phase.

Pass condition: any one of the realization's listed denial signals, asserted as an expectation, satisfies the automated check; the concrete signal list (denial status codes, unauthorised/forbidden/denied/permission wording, rejection or throw assertions) is realization detail.

Automated check behaviour: it identifies security tests by URN and flags those whose body contains no denial assertion. Binding of the denial to the acceptance's protected operation, and the protected-effect witness, are not detected mechanically — they are reviewer-judged.

The automated finding is non-gating for review: the acceptance-bound review (protected-operation binding and protected-effect witness) applies to every security test even when the automated check reports nothing.

fires: A test whose URN carries a -SEC- kind segment and whose body only asserts a successful response (e.g. 200) (automated check and review).
A test with an -AUTH- or -RLS- URN kind segment whose expectations contain none of the realization's listed denial signals (automated check and review).
A security-URN test that asserts the denial on an unrelated operation rather than on the bound protected operation (acceptance-bound review only; the automated check passes it).
A security-URN test for a protected mutation that asserts the denial but never checks that the mutation did not happen (acceptance-bound review only).
An existing, unchanged security-URN test examined during an audit or review.
doesNotFire: A test whose URN kind segment is not SEC, RLS or AUTH, even if its filename contains 'auth' or 'security'.
A SEC/RLS/AUTH test whose denial case asserts the refusal of the bound protected operation (and, for a protected side effect, that it did not occur), with or without an extra happy-path case.

profileRequirements.meaning: How a test file binds itself to the acceptance URN from whose kind segment (SEC, RLS, AUTH) it is identified as a security test; the binding declared in the file is authoritative over the filename.
profileRequirements.bunValue: the URN kind segment (-SEC-, -RLS-, -AUTH-) is read from the test header; the header, not the filename, is authoritative

bunOnly.text: language: [typescript, javascript], observable_now — 'Bun test runner realization.'
bunOnly.reason: A realization-specific language gate on which files this detector scans (the languages of the stack's test files). The closed vocabulary's tooling.languages covers production-source languages only, so no existing key carries this meaning, and the neutral core does not gate on language; the gate re-enters on instantiation as this bunOnly fact.

bunOnly.text: `const res = await fetch("/orders", { method: "POST" });   // anonymous` then `expect(res.status).toBe(403);` (status only; for a protected mutation add the unchanged-state check above).
bunOnly.reason: Concrete code in the runtime's fetch API and the test runner's expect matcher; the core keeps examples role-level, and bun.json itself is delivered as the worked reference example.

bunOnly.text: an expectation tied to 401, 403, unauthorised, forbidden, denied, permission, `.rejects` or `toThrow`
bunOnly.reason: The concrete denial-signal token list — including the test-runner matcher APIs `.rejects` and `toThrow` — is the Bun detector's scan list; the core defers to "the realization's listed denial signals".
Validator/detector ids of this one rule are realization details; the core's verification describes the check generically.

bunOnly.reason: The finding id names this stack's detector; the neutral semantics (non-gating; the acceptance-bound review applies even when the check reports nothing) are kept in core verification.

neutralityNotes: The concrete denial-signal token list (401, 403, unauthorised, forbidden, denied, permission, and the `.rejects`/`toThrow` matcher APIs) could not be made neutral: it is the Bun detector's scan list, so the core says 'the realization's listed denial signals' and defers the enumeration to the realization; 401/403 survive in `then` and `fires` only as protocol-level examples, never as stack names. Identifying a security test by URN kind segment (SEC/RLS/AUTH) is ATDD-level and stays in the core; the concrete binding syntax (the header comment) enters only through the profile key urn.binding.acceptance. Language gating (typescript/javascript) is a realization-specific fact of this detector: the closed vocabulary's tooling.languages covers production-source languages only, so the Bun language fact is preserved as a bunOnly activation fact (the neutral core does not gate on language) rather than routed through a mismatched or newly proposed key. Detector, validator and finding ids of this rule are bunOnly, and severity 4 / disposition strict are carried in core verification, per the closed vocabulary's notProfileKeys. No vocabulary key was missing, so proposedKeys is empty.
